```markdown
Avery Hayes
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
Member ID: W671125198

[Date]

Wellpoint
Appeals Department
[Appeal address exactly as printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-09**
**Member: Avery Hayes | Member ID: W671125198**
**Reference number: POC-1F29AC6C03-84154**
**Service denied: Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702**
**Governing policy: Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon) — https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf**

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the total ankle replacement (CPT 27702) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-09 states that the records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the plan's own published criteria are addressed in my medical records. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I set out the plan's criteria in its own words and point to what my records show.

---

## 1. The plan's overall standard

The guideline states:

> "Total ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

I address each criterion the plan has published, beginning with the one the denial is based on.

## 2. Conservative management — the reason given for the denial

The plan's criterion reads:

> "Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management"

My records document conservative care well beyond three months, and document that pain and impairment persisted afterward:

- **NSAID therapy for 8 months**, with inadequate relief.
- **Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08**, which gave three weeks of partial relief.
- **Supervised physical therapy from 2026-05-08 to 2026-07-03 — 8 weeks, 24 visits completed**, focused on ankle strengthening and balance, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Symptoms have been present for **18 months of progressive ankle pain, unrelieved by rest**.

After all of that treatment, my pain and my limitations remain. I still walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to about two blocks, and my range of motion is limited by pain on examination.

The plan also states:

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

and

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My chart contains each of these elements: symptom duration (18 months), the specific functional limitation (walking limited to two blocks, antalgic gait), and the type and duration of every therapeutic measure (8 months of NSAIDs, an injection on 2026-05-08, and 24 supervised physical therapy visits over 8 weeks). Compliance is documented by the completed 24-visit course and the discharge note.

One further criterion in the guideline reads:

> "Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of complementary strategies that I do not have in front of me, so I cannot match my care to items I have not been shown. My documented care includes supervised physical therapy, NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection. If the plan based its denial on the footwear or accommodative-device element, or on a specific item from the list that follows this sentence, I ask the plan to identify in writing exactly which criterion it applied and what it found missing, and I will ask my treating providers to supply the corresponding records: [documentation of footwear modification, padding, or foot orthosis, if provided — to be completed from the chart].

## 3. Radiographic and imaging criteria

The plan requires:

> "Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint"

> "Imaging report. The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months. In the absence of a detailed report, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

> "Imaging reports should describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, or avascular necrosis. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted."

Weight-bearing ankle radiographs obtained **2026-07-13** — within the past twelve months — show **tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts**. Those findings are in the same joint that hurts, and they correlate with my clinical findings of positive provocative testing on the affected side, range of motion limited by pain, and an antalgic gait.

## 4. Pain and functional impairment as the plan defines them

The plan defines the terms this way:

> "For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes."

My records document walking as a clearly impacted daily activity: I have an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks. For the pain rating and any additional impacted activity, I ask the plan to review [VAS pain score(s) as recorded in the office notes of Dr. Duval — to be completed from the chart] and [any additional impacted daily activities documented in the office notes — to be completed from the chart]. I am not going to state numbers that I cannot point to in my own records.

## 5. Vascular perfusion

The plan requires:

> "Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses)"

I ask the plan to review [the pedal pulse / vascular examination findings recorded in Dr. Duval's examination note — to be completed from the chart]. If this documentation was not included in the original submission, I ask that the plan request it rather than deny the surgery on that basis.

## 6. Recommended pre-surgical factors

The guideline also states:

> "Tobacco cessation. Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended."

> "It is strongly recommended that a patient with a history of diabetes maintain a hemoglobin A1C of 8% or less prior to any joint replacement surgery."

> "Body Mass Index (BMI). It is strongly recommended that any patient with a BMI equal to or greater than 40 attempt weight reduction prior to surgery."

My records show that I am a **non-smoker** and that my **BMI is 29**. My records also show **no active infection and no untreated substance use**.

---

## What I am asking for

I am asking Wellpoint to overturn the denial of CPT 27702 and authorize the total ankle replacement recommended by Dr. Duval. In the alternative, if the plan maintains the denial, I ask that it provide me in writing:

1. the specific criterion or criteria from the Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon) that it found unmet;
2. the full text of the list that follows the conservative-management sentence quoted above, so that I can respond to it; and
3. the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination.

I also request that any records the plan believes are missing be requested from Dr. Duval's office and from my physical therapy provider before a final decision is made. I am happy to sign any authorization needed to release them.

Per the denial notice, this appeal must be received by **2027-02-05** (180 days from the 2026-08-09 date of notice). I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I can also be reached at the phone number and email listed below if anything further is needed to process this appeal.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I am not asking for an exception to the rules — I am asking the plan to apply its own published criteria to what is already in my chart.

Sincerely,

**Avery Hayes**
Member ID: W671125198
Reference number: POC-1F29AC6C03-84154
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date signed]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-09
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-08 to 2026-07-03, 24 visits)
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report dated 2026-07-13
- Office notes from Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery
- [Any additional records to be listed]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
```
